title: Ang 1000–1019: Guru Arjan and ashtpadis
tomorrow: should a hymn be read in Gurmukhi, or in words everyone gets?

segments.voice: Yesterday, ang 990: the body is paper, the mind is the writing, and real silver rings true. Brave faith. Today, a riddle about money that isn't about money.

Two people awake at two in the morning, both staring at the ceiling. One got three job offers and can't choose; every option feels like losing the other two. The other is doing the math on rent again. Opposite problems, same ceiling. Guru Arjan saw both of them. Near the end of these pages, on ang 1019, he writes a line that sounds like a riddle: the house with plenty is full of worry, and the house with little wanders around searching. So who, exactly, gets to sleep?
screen: `TWO PEOPLE, ONE CEILING.` → `PLENTY WORRIES. LITTLE WANDERS.` → `SO WHO SLEEPS?`

segments.voice: First, where we are. These pages of Maru carry more of Guru Arjan's hymns, the fifth Guru, and ashtpadis, longer hymns built in eight-stanza runs. Then, on ang 1019, a set of Guru Arjan's hymns headed Anjulian, a word tied to cupped hands, the way you'd hold out your palms to receive something. And that's where the riddle sits. In paraphrase: in the house where there is much, there is worry; in the house where there is little, a person wanders, searching. The one who is free of both conditions is the one found at ease. Here's the twist. The Guru doesn't say get rich, and he doesn't say get poor. He doesn't pick a side at all. Both houses lose sleep, because in both, the amount is in charge. Plenty has to be guarded. Little has to be chased. The ease belongs to the one who isn't ruled by either, who holds out cupped hands and takes what comes. That takes nerve. It's easier to believe one more raise would fix it, or that nothing could. So Maru keeps doing what Maru does: it asks for courage, this time the courage to stop letting the number run the night. More courage.
screen: `GURU ARJAN AND THE ASHTPADIS.` · `ANJULIAN: CUPPED HANDS.` · `PLENTY WORRIES, LITTLE WANDERS.` · `FREE OF BOTH, AT EASE.` · then, large: `MORE COURAGE.`

segments.voice: Rest your hands open in your lap, palms up, like cupped hands waiting. On your fingers, slowly count things you already have that are enough for today: a meal, a bed, one person who'd pick up the phone. When you run out of fingers, just keep the palms open and breathe.
Ang 1000. Where more of Guru Arjan's Maru hymns begin, leading on to the Anjulian and the riddle of the two houses.
For the road: more courage, enough to stop letting the number run the night. Day fifteen-seventy, palms up.
